summary.text: Huizenga is the incumbent U.S. Representative, first elected in 2010 to represent Michigan's then-2nd District and representing the current 4th District since redistricting took effect in 2023. A co-owner of a family gravel business, he worked as a realtor and as a congressional aide, and served in the Michigan House of Representatives before running for Congress. In the 119th Congress he is vice chair of the House Financial Services Committee and chairs its Foreign Affairs subcommittee on South and Central Asia.

paragraphs.text: Bill Huizenga was born January 31, 1969, in Zeeland, Michigan; according to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Ottawa County. He graduated from Holland Christian High School in 1987 and earned a B.A. in political science from Calvin College in 1991.

According to his House biography, he began his career as a realtor and entrepreneur; Wikipedia dates his real estate work to the early 1990s. He co-owns Huizenga Gravel Inc., a family business in Jenison, Michigan, and his campaign website describes him as a third-generation small business owner.
From 1997 to 2003, Huizenga worked as Director of Public Policy for then-U.S. Rep. Pete Hoekstra (R).
He was elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (90th District, Ottawa County) in 2002 and re-elected in 2004 and 2006, after which he was term-limited.

When Hoekstra left the seat to run for governor, Huizenga won the 2010 Republican primary for Michigan's 2nd District, then won the general election over Democrat Fred Johnson, 64% to 32%. He has been re-elected in each cycle since.

In the 119th Congress Huizenga is vice chair of the House Financial Services Committee, chairs the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia and sits on its Africa subcommittee. In the 118th Congress he chaired the Financial Services Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

Since 2017 he has been elected by colleagues as a co-chair of the bipartisan Great Lakes Task Force, and he is the Republican co-chair of the Bipartisan Fiscal Forum, a group focused on the federal debt.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Ottawa County with his wife, Natalie, and their five children.
